title: CCD shift register, optical line scanning and area imaging
outcome: The 1970 eight-bit register produced an optical image and supplied an electrode design for Bell’s 96-element line imager. By September 1972 the Bell team was reporting images made with an electronically scanned area array.
findings: The existing April 1970 verification report measures electronic transfer between MOS capacitors. The August report documents the separate eight-stage integrated CCD, with electrical injection and serial diode readout in shift-register mode. Its abstract also reports optical line scanning, and Smith’s later first-person lecture reproduces the image on an oscilloscope.

The 1971 96-element report explicitly identifies the eight-bit register as a design precedent for the three-phase connections via metallization and a diffused crossunder. Figure 4 shows printed text and Figure 5 shows a grayscale reproduction, both made using mechanical scanning across the line sensor.

The 1971 line-imager paper’s Figure 7 proposes an area imager with a frame store. The area team explicitly credits this design in the later technical paper. At the 22 September 1972 NASA symposium Séquin showed the result of imaging with the 128-by-106 array. The 1973 technical paper shows actual images in separate whole-array and frame-transfer modes.

The 18 January 1973 Electronics article documents a laboratory camera that split the scene into red, green and blue for three CCD sensors. Its cover includes the image of Margaret Tompsett. The camera is a separate system demonstration. The contemporary citation dates the report and does not fix the date of the exposure or identify the exact three chips.
frontier: Obtain the full APL paper 10.1063/1.1653327, pp. 111–115, to check the original optical target, optics and readout procedure. Compare the original plates against the oscilloscope image in Smith’s lecture.

Read the original March 1972 INTERCON digest pp. 292–293 for the distinct 8-by-15 area device cited on p. 244 of the later IEEE article. Determine exactly what was presented and whether an optical image survives.

Check lab or demonstration logs for the three-CCD color camera and cover portrait, including exact capture date and the source of the inconsistent array dimensions in the January 1973 cover caption and technical text.

screen: Compared the canonical Boyle–Smith concept and April verification event, Bell 96-element imager, Bell buried-channel CCD, Fairchild CCD101 and Kodak camera. No matching integrated eight-stage register or 128-by-106 frame-transfer area imager was found in the discovery and lead indexes.
limits: The 1970 exact optical capture date and original apparatus details remain unresolved. The 1972 result dates a symposium report of a working area device and a reproduced image. The camera and sensors produced analog video in the demonstrations described. Worldwide priority, digitization, commercial sale and astronomical adoption are outside these records.
